# hdrs


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

For inline assets, pass `reg.hdrs()` and `reg.ftrs()` to `FastHTML` or
`fast_app`. The headers include the shared foundation stylesheet,
registered application rules, the delegated event script, and the shared
browser helpers. The footer includes the `fastlucide` icon
`spritesheet`. FastHTML renders the registry’s current rules on each
response, including rules registered after app creation. To serve cached
local asset URLs instead, call `reg.serve(app)`. It mounts the asset
routes and appends the headers and footers to `app`.

``` python
from fasthtml.common import *
from answerui.registry import reg, hypelt
from fastcore.test import *
from fastlucide.icons import Check
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
```

`assets` caches the compiled stylesheet and script because building the
stylesheet walks every rule. The registry increments `version` on each
change. `assets` rebuilds only when `version` differs from its cached
build:

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Registry.assets

``` python
def assets():
```

*The stylesheet and script, keyed by extension, built once per registry
version*

`assets` returns the same build until a rule changes:

``` python
r = Registry()
built = r.assets()
test_is(r.assets(), built)
r.rule('main { max-width: 65ch; }', 'page')
assert r.assets() is not built
assert 'max-width: 65ch' in r.assets()['css']
list(built)
```

    ['css', 'js']

FastHTML calls `__ft__` on each object that defines it. `_Lazy` uses
that hook to render the registry’s current CSS and event script on each
response. For inline pages and notebook previews, `_inline_browser`
rewrites `browser.js` so its imports of `floating.js`,
`interactions.js`, `fit.js`, and `copy.js` use base64 `data:` URLs
rather than relative paths. On served pages, the browser loads those
same files over HTTP. If your app uses its own `Registry`, pass its
`hdrs()` instead of `reg.hdrs()`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Registry.hdrs

``` python
def hdrs():
```

*Inline foundation, application rules and browser behavior, rendered
from this registry per response*

To see that the headers are lazy, build them first and define a
component afterwards. Rendering the stylesheet header then includes the
component’s CSS.

``` python
hdrs = reg.hdrs()
LateCard = hypelt('LateCard', css='display: block; color: teal;', layer='components',
    on={('&', 'click'): r"el.remove()"}, doc='Defined after the app; click to remove.')
css = to_xml(hdrs[0])
print(css[css.index('/* LateCard.base */'):][:60])
```

    /* LateCard.base */
    late-card {
    display: block; color: teal;

Redefining the component changes the next render. There is no rebuild
step and nothing to invalidate:

``` python
LateCard = hypelt('LateCard', css='display: block; color: navy;', layer='components', doc='Defined after the app.')
css = to_xml(hdrs[0])
assert 'navy' in css and 'teal' not in css
```

Each icon references a symbol in `fastlucide`’s `spritesheet`. Importing
an icon from `fastlucide.icons` adds its symbol to `spritesheet`.
Because `spritesheet` is an `<svg>` element, it belongs in `<body>`
rather than `<head>`. `ftrs` returns `(spritesheet,)` for FastHTML to
render at the end of `<body>`. Because `spritesheet` already defines
`__ft__` for per-page rendering, `ftrs` returns it directly without a
`_Lazy` wrapper:

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Registry.ftrs

``` python
def ftrs():
```

*Footers for `fast_app(ftrs=...)`: fastlucide’s sprite sheet, with every
icon that any module has imported*

## A whole page

FastHTML’s test `Client` fetches a page without starting a server. In
the response, `<head>` contains `htmx`, the AnswerUI stylesheet, the
event script, and the inline `browser.js` module. The `spritesheet`
appears at the end of `<body>`, after the icon that references it.

``` python
app = FastHTML(hdrs=reg.hdrs(), ftrs=reg.ftrs())
rt = app.route

@rt
def index(): return Titled('Hello', LateCard(Check(), 'Defined after the app.'))

page = Client(app).get('/').text
assert page.index('<symbol id="lc-check"') > page.index('late-card')
print(re.sub(r'(?s)(<(style|script)\b[^>]*>).*?(?=</\2>)', r'\1…', page))
```

    <!doctype html>
    <html>
      <head>
        <title>Hello</title>
        <link rel="canonical" href="https://testserver/">
        <meta charset="utf-8">
        <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1, viewport-fit=cover">
    <script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/htmx.org@2.0.7/dist/htmx.js">…</script><script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/answerdotai/fasthtml-js@1.0.13/fasthtml.js">…</script><script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/answerdotai/surreal@main/surreal.js">…</script><script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/gnat/css-scope-inline@main/script.js">…</script>    <style>…</style>
    <script>…</script><script type="module">…</script>  </head>
      <body>
    <main class="container">      <h1>Hello</h1>
    <late-card><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewbox="0 0 24 24" height="24px" width="24px" class="lucide-icon "><use href="#lc-check"></use></svg>Defined after the app.</late-card></main>    <style>…</style>
    <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" style="display: none"><defs><symbol id="lc-check"><path d="M20 6 9 17l-5-5"></path></symbol></defs></svg>  </body>
    </html>

With `fast_app`, pass `pico=False` to disable Pico CSS:

``` python
app, rt = fast_app(hdrs=reg.hdrs(), ftrs=reg.ftrs(), pico=False)
@rt
def index(): return Titled('Hello', LateCard('Defined after the app.'))

assert 'pico' not in (r:= Client(app).get('/').text)
assert 'late-card' in r
```

## Serving the assets

Call `reg.serve(app)` instead of passing `reg.hdrs()` and `reg.ftrs()`
to serve cached assets from local URLs under `path` (default
`/answerui`). `serve` mounts content-hashed routes for the stylesheet
and event script with
`Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`. Each registry
version is built once. The asset handler continues to serve the original
bytes for earlier hashed URLs and returns 404 for unknown names. Because
the handler builds the current version on demand, a separate worker
process can serve the current assets without rendering a page first.

`serve` also mounts the packaged asset tree (`browser.js`, its helper
modules, optional `fonts.css`, and font files) under a URL prefix hashed
from the whole tree. Relative module imports and font URLs resolve under
that prefix. `serve` appends the headers to `app.hdrs` and `spritesheet`
to `app.ftrs`. It also returns the header tuple in case you assemble
`<head>` manually.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Registry.serve

``` python
def serve(
    app, # The FastHTML app to mount the route on and add the headers to
    path:str='/answerui', # URL prefix the assets are served under
):
```

*Serve content-hashed assets, adding their headers and the icon sprite
sheet to `app`; returns the headers*

``` python
app, worker = FastHTML(), FastHTML()
rt = app.route
for a in (app, worker): reg.serve(a)

@rt
def index(): return Titled('Hello', LateCard('Defined after the app.'))

page = Client(app).get('/').text
href = re.search(r'href="(/answerui/[^"]+\.css)"', page)[1]
asset = Client(worker).get(href)
test_eq(asset.headers['cache-control'], 'public, max-age=31536000, immutable')
assert 'navy' in asset.text
href
```

    '/answerui/1221d56a19a8.css'

After a registry change, the next page links to a new hashed URL.
Requesting the previous URL still returns the earlier build. Requesting
an unknown URL returns 404:

``` python
LateCard = hypelt('LateCard', css='display: block; color: teal;', layer='components', doc='Defined after the app.')
href2 = re.search(r'href="(/answerui/[^"]+\.css)"', Client(app).get('/').text)[1]
assert href2 != href
assert 'navy' in Client(app).get(href).text
assert 'teal' in Client(app).get(href2).text
test_eq(Client(app).get('/answerui/000000000000.css').status_code, 404)
```

CSS rules sometimes reference external files, such as a font or logo.
Register a file with `reg.file(name, path, url)` and use the returned
URL in your rule. `serve` mounts the file at a content-hashed URL under
`path` and rewrites the public URL in the stylesheet and script. Without
`serve`, the browser fetches the file from the public URL.

``` python
r, tmp = Registry(), TemporaryDirectory()
logo = Path(tmp.name)/'logo.svg'
logo.write_text('<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"/>')
url = r.file('logo.svg', logo, 'https://example.com/logo.svg')
r.rule(f"header {{ background: url('{url}'); }}", 'brand')
assert url in r.build_css()
```

The stylesheet’s hashed URL is computed from its rewritten content,
including each local file URL. Another worker process can serve the
app’s copy of the file without rendering a page first:

``` python
app, worker = FastHTML(), FastHTML()
for a in (app, worker): r.serve(a)

@app.get('/')
def index(): return Titled('Hello')

cli = Client(app)
css_href = re.search(r'href="(/answerui/[^"]+\.css)"', cli.get('/').text)[1]
css = cli.get(css_href).text
test_eq(css_href, f'/answerui/{_hash(css)}.css')
assert url not in css
served_logo = re.search(r"url\('(/answerui/\w+-logo\.svg)'\)", css)[1]
test_eq(Client(worker).get(served_logo).text, logo.read_text())
served_logo
```

    '/answerui/900fbe934249-logo.svg'
